luke.6.p1.b1.text: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields,

luke.6.p1.b2.text: and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them.

luke.6.p1.b3.text: “Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”

luke.6.p2.b1.text: “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?

luke.6.p2.b2.text: He entered the house of God, took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions,

luke.6.p2.b3.text: and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat.”

luke.6.p2.b4.text: “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”

luke.6.p3.b1.text: On another Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was withered.

luke.6.p3.b2.text: Looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, the scribes and Pharisees were watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.

luke.6.p3.b4.text: So he got up and stood there.

luke.6.p4.b1.text: “I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”

luke.6.p4.b3.text: He did so, and it was restored.

luke.6.p4.b4.text: But the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus.

luke.6.p5.b1.text: In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray,

luke.6.p5.b2.text: and He spent the night in prayer to God.

luke.6.p5.b4.text: He called His disciples to Him

luke.6.p6.b1.text: and chose twelve of them, whom He also designated as apostles:

luke.6.p6.b2.text: Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John;

luke.6.p6.b3.text: Philip and Bartholomew; Matthew and Thomas;

luke.6.p6.b4.text: James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot; Judas son of James,

luke.6.p6.b5.text: and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.

luke.6.p7.b1.text: Then Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place.

luke.6.p7.b2.text: … a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon.

luke.6.p7.b3.text: They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases, and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.

luke.6.p7.b4.text: The entire crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was coming from Him and healing them all.

luke.6.p8.b1.text: Looking up at His disciples, Jesus said:

luke.6.p8.b2.text: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.

luke.6.p8.b3.text: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled.

luke.6.p8.b4.text: Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.

luke.6.p9.b1.text: Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.

luke.6.p9.b2.text: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven.

luke.6.p9.b3.text: For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.

luke.6.p10.b1.text: But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.

luke.6.p10.b2.text: Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger.

luke.6.p10.b3.text: Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.

luke.6.p10.b4.text: Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.

luke.6.p11.b1.text: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,

luke.6.p11.b2.text: If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also.

luke.6.p11.b3.text: And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.

luke.6.p11.b4.text: Do to others as you would have them do to you.

luke.6.p12.b1.text: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.

luke.6.p12.b2.text: But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great,

luke.6.p12.b3.text: and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.

luke.6.p12.b4.text: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

luke.6.p13.b1.text: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned.

luke.6.p13.b2.text: Forgive, and you will be forgiven.

luke.6.p13.b3.text: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap.

luke.6.p13.b4.text: For with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”

luke.6.p14.b1.text: Jesus also told them a parable:

luke.6.p14.b2.text: “Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?

luke.6.p14.b3.text: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

luke.6.p14.b4.text: You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

luke.6.p15.b1.text: No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.

luke.6.p15.b2.text: Indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes,

luke.6.p15.b4.text: For out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks.

luke.6.p16.b1.text: Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but not do what I say?

luke.6.p16.b2.text: He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock.

luke.6.p16.b3.text: When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.

luke.6.p16.b4.text: The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell—and great was its destruction!”
